question: Yoga should help lower blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar, all of whom can harm your heart and blood vessels.

options.A: Yoga should help lower blood pressure,
options.D: all of whom can harm your heart and blood vessels.

solution.incorrectPart: all of whom can harm your heart and blood vessels.
solution.correctPart: all of which can harm your heart and blood vessels.
explanation: Which is used to refer to things or non-human nouns.
Whom is used to refer to people as the object of a verb or preposition.
Blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar are things, not people.
Correct sentence: Yoga should help lower blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar, all of which can harm your heart and blood vessels.

question: A founder's goal, during the first phase, is to learn how to obtain feedback on how prospective and real customers are experience the product.

options.A: A founder's goal, during the first
options.B: phase, is to learn how to
options.C: obtain feedback on how prospective and
options.D: real customers are experience the product.

solution.incorrectPart: real customers are experience the product.
solution.correctPart: real customers are experiencing the product.
explanation: The auxiliary verb are must be followed by the present participle (verb + ing) to form the present continuous tense.
Alternatively, experience can be used in the simple present tense without "are".
Correct sentence: A founder's goal, during the first phase, is to learn how to obtain feedback on how prospective and real customers are experiencing the product.

question: In many low and middle income countries, health coverage has improved dramatically in the last two but health outcomes may not.

options.A: In many low and middle income
options.B: countries, health coverage has improved dramatically

explanation: The word decades is missing. The phrase "in the last two" is incomplete because the time period is not specified.
Correct sentence: In many low- and middle-income countries, health coverage has improved dramatically in the last two decades, but health outcomes may not.

question: Since you have been found guilty for delivering poor results for six months at a stretch, we are issuing this warning letter to warn you.

options.A: Since you have been found guilty for
options.B: delivering poor results for six months
options.C: at a stretch, we are issuing
options.D: this warning letter to warn you.

solution.incorrectPart: Since you have been found guilty for
solution.correctPart: Since you have been found guilty of
explanation: The adjective guilty is generally followed by the preposition of, not for, when referring to wrongdoing or an offence.
Guilty – Of; Accused – Of; Capable – Of; Responsible – For; Famous – For; Interested – In.
Correct sentence: Since you have been found guilty of delivering poor results for six months at a stretch, we are issuing this warning letter to warn you.

question: Today, researchers are trying to establish whether yoga must help relieve depression and arthritis.

explanation: Must expresses necessity or strong obligation.
May expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Correct sentence: Today, researchers are trying to establish whether yoga may help relieve depression and arthritis.

question: It helps anyone whom wants to enter into a contractual relationship with the company to gain knowledge about the company.

explanation: Who is used as the subject of a verb.
Whom is used as the object of a verb or preposition.
Quick trick: If you can replace the word with he/she, use who. If you can replace it with him/her, use whom.
Correct sentence: It helps anyone who wants to enter into a contractual relationship with the company to gain knowledge about the company.

question: We live in an ever changed world and in order to keep up and become successful, continuous education is a must.

options.A: We live in an ever changed

solution.incorrectPart: We live in an ever changed
solution.correctPart: We live in an ever changing
explanation: When describing something that changes continuously, use the present participle changing as an adjective.
Correct sentence: We live in an ever-changing world, and in order to keep up and become successful, continuous education is a must.

question: The search for better employment opportunities are the key mechanism by which the majority of the world's population can hope to improve their lives.

options.A: The search for better employment opportunities
options.B: are the key mechanism by which
options.C: the majority of the world's population
options.D: can hope to improve their lives.

solution.incorrectPart: are the key mechanism by which
solution.correctPart: is the key mechanism by which
explanation: The subject of the sentence is "The search", which is singular.
Do not get confused by "better employment opportunities" because it is part of the prepositional phrase describing the search.
Correct sentence: The search for better employment opportunities is the key mechanism by which the majority of the world's population can hope to improve their lives.

question: One scorching summer, the desert became dry, and there was no water left for the plants. The rose quickly begin to wilt.

options.A: One scorching summer, the desert became
options.B: dry, and there was no water

explanation: The sentence describes an event that happened in the past (One scorching summer, the desert became dry).  Therefore, the verb should also be in the simple past tense.
Exam tip: When a sentence describes a past event, check whether all the main verbs maintain the appropriate past tense.
Correct sentence: One scorching summer, the desert became dry, and there was no water left for the plants. The rose quickly began to wilt.

question: We use essential cookies to make our site work. With your consent, we may also uses non-essential cookies to improve user experience and analyze website traffic.

options.A: We use essential cookies to make our
options.B: site work. With your consent, we may
options.D: to improve user experience and analyze website traffic.

explanation: After a modal verb such as may, can, could, should, must, we always use the base form (V1) of the main verb.
Correct sentence: We use essential cookies to make our site work. With your consent, we may also use non-essential cookies to improve user experience and analyze website traffic.
